title: GPU page saturation causing runtime KV zipper corruption across hosted/dedicated/private - patch, mitigation & rollout
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported high-rate GPU OOMs followed by persistent KV cache corruption observed as "zipper" mismatches during KV compaction/reconcile. This ticket tracks investigation, an interim mitigation, the runtime patch, testing, and rollout plan. The behavior only appears under sustained high-concurrency prefix caching with long-lived sessions and heavy eviction churn.
reproduction_steps: 2) Run on a 4xA100 node with rw-mount and enable preemption to simulate noisy neighbors,
3) Observe GPU resident set growth until OOM, then run 'tools/kv-verify --scan-all --consistency-check' to detect zipper mismatches
4) Reproduce locally in dedicated environment and then validate on a hosted canary namespace.
investigation_findings: Timeline: initial customer alert (2026-03-08) -> triage & alerting tweaks (03-09) -> root cause narrowed (03-11). Findings: the runtime's session allocator uses a 32-bit page reference counter inside the KV handle coalescer. Under continuous prefix caching with tens of thousands of small allocations, refcount increments overflowed and truncated during concurrent compaction. This allowed two compaction threads to believe a page was free and both link it into different KV shards (the 'zipper' mismatch). Concurrent GPU page reclamation under heavy kernel preemption made the window narrow and non-deterministic, manifesting as intermittent corruption and then rapid OOM cascades when duplicated references freed the same physical page twice. Secondary contributing factor: compaction scheduling allowed compaction to start when GPU memory pressure was only nominally high, increasing concurrency of evict/compact cycles.
mitigations_taken: 2026-03-09: Enabled stricter alerting for KV zipper checks in hosted (added kv_zipper_failure metric).
2026-03-10: Deployed temporary rate-limiter for prefix-cache writes for affected customers (reduces incoming session cache churn).
2026-03-11: Enabled emergency pre-eviction sweep: single-threaded compact loop for canary hosts to avoid concurrent compactions.
2026-03-12: Rolling fallback route: route high-risk requests to CPU-backed model pool for impacted tenants while patch is validated.
fix_summary: Runtime patch changes the page reference counter from 32-bit to 64-bit atomics, adds a lightweight compaction fence to serialize final link/unlink steps of the KV zipper coalescer, and introduces a short backoff (50-200ms randomized) before a compaction retries after eviction to avoid tight cross-thread races. Also adjusts compaction scheduling policy to avoid starting compaction under marginal GPU pressure and adds an extra validation pass that detects duplicate physical page attachments before finalize (safety-check).
testing_plan: Unit: new atomic refcount tests + injected overflow test vectors
Integration: 'runtime_kv_saturator' extended to include deterministic race injection harness (CI job runtime-kv-race-4xA100)
Staging: 48-hour soak in dedicated staging with canonical workload sets from three customers (LLM-chat, long-context summarization, embedding-batch)
Canary: Gradual rollout to 5% hosted namespaces -> 20% -> 100% with tight SLO and kv_zipper_failure gating
Backwards compatibility: runtime will detect older session metadata and run a migration sweep at startup (non-blocking).
rollout_steps: 2) Deploy to internal dogfood cluster with emergency pre-evict disabled and run 24h soak
3) Canary deploy to low-risk hosted namespaces (5%) with automatic rollback if kv_zipper_failure rate > 0.05% or GPU OOM alerts spike by >3s compared to baseline
4) After 72h canary stable, ramp to Dedicated customer pools with opt-in by account owners for first 48h,
5) Coordinate with Private deployment customers; provide patch package and migration checklist and schedule maintenance windows for on-prem upgrades
postmortem_action_items: A: Replace remaining 32-bit counters in allocator codepath (owner: runtime-allocator team, estimate 5)
B: Add kv_zipper_failure alert to P1 alerting with runbook (owner: observability, estimate 2)
C: Improve preemption-sim test coverage in CI to catch GPU kernel preemption races (owner: infra, estimate 3)
D: Create a customer communication bundle and FAQ for Dedicated/Private upgrade windows (owner: customer-success, estimate 2)
E: Quarterly audit of compaction heuristics and stress testing with real customer traces (owner: research, estimate 8)
F: Post-release soak report and SLA credit analysis if any affected customers breached latency/SLO (owner: reliability-eng, estimate 3)
